verdict:
KILL. The loudest bull claim is management's own reaffirmed guide, and the two-year comp stack says it is unattainable - which the triage established from pre-print filings alone, before any court.

THE ONE-YEAR COMPS LOOK LIKE A RECOVERY AND THE STACK SAYS THE OPPOSITE. FY24 ran -5.6 / -6.3 / -7.7 / -9.4 and FY25 ran -8.3 / -3.0 / -4.0 / -3.3, with FY26 Q1 at -5.4. Read singly, the trend improved. Stacked two-year: -9.3 (Q2 FY25) then -11.7 then -12.7 then -13.7 (Q1 FY26) - deteriorating three consecutive quarters, back to the cycle worst of -13.9. Nine consecutive quarters of negative comps, four consecutive EPS misses (-$0.38, -$0.74, -$0.06, -$0.52), adjusted EBITDA down in both FY25 ($436.6M against $506.2M) and Q1 FY26 ($123.2M against $136.1M). The CEO staked FY2026 on being 'highly confident in our ability to drive positive comps for the remainder of the year while generating over $100 million in free cash flow'.

AND Q2 FY26 IS THE HARDEST LAP OF THE YEAR, NOT THE EASIEST. Q2 laps -3.0%, the SOFTEST prior-year print of the last eight quarters, which means it is the hardest comparison. Holding the Q1 FY26 two-year stack flat at -13.7 implies Q2 FY26 comps of about -10.7%. Reverting all the way to the best stack of the last five quarters (-9.3) still implies about -6.3%. To print merely ZERO, the stack must improve 10.7 points in a single quarter - a swing with no precedent anywhere in the two-year record. There is no calendar alibi either: Easter 2026 (April 5) and Easter 2025 (April 20) both fall inside Q1, and the company states comps on a same-calendar-period basis.

THE EXCESS DRAWDOWN IS CAPITAL STRUCTURE, NOT DISPERSION. The -42.9-point excess versus the sector median is leverage mechanics: $1,535.3M of face debt at 3.3x net total leverage against a $343M market cap means equity is about 18% of enterprise value, so a -13.7% move in EBITDA becomes a -60% move in the equity. That is arithmetic. A sector-excess drawdown screen firing on a levered stub is measuring the capital structure, not a mispricing, and it will keep doing so.

GOVERNANCE IS THE aggravating factor: the second CEO exit in twenty months, with Tarun Lal retiring on 2026-08-03 SEVEN WEEKS after reaffirming the guide; CFO Darin Harper promoted to CEO; and the Head of Entertainment Finance, Cory Hatton, serving as INTERIM CFO into the print. A first-week CEO and an interim CFO hold the pen on the reset. Entry now buys a levered stub into a print whose own guide-metric the stack says is unreachable, at +13.1% off the $9.40 low.

THE BULL'S ONE CLEAN DATUM SURVIVES AND SHOULD BE STATED: adjusted free cash flow inflected to +$25.3M from -$58.8M, liquidity is $499.1M, and the maturity wall is 2029/2031, so there is no 2026-2028 refinancing event. This is not a solvency story and should never be argued as one. But that free cash flow is being manufactured by cutting growth capex - which is precisely what caps the comp recovery it is supposed to fund. That is the same improvement-bought-not-earned pattern BLDP shows in this batch, in a different sector.

That would make the damage-absent case live for the first time in nine quarters and re-scores the name to >=7.

DATA: a company press release CONFIRMING the actual print date. Everything in the record is fiscal-calendar reconstruction plus a third-party estimate that itself states the company has not confirmed.
OPERATIONAL: evidence that free cash flow is being generated WITHOUT further growth-capex cuts. Today the FCF inflection and the comp decline are the same decision.
GOVERNANCE: a permanent CFO appointment. A first-week CEO plus an interim CFO writing the guidance reset is not a stable basis for underwriting any forward number.
